references.text: Frankincense (levona) is mentioned as part of the incense in the sanctuary and highlights the ritual use of pure frankincense in worshiping the Lord.

With the grain offering, frankincense was to be placed on the flour, and the priest was to burn the memorial portion (azkara) as a fire offering to the Lord, just like the frankincense on the bread of the Presence.
The memorial portion (azkara), together with all the frankincense, is burned as a fire offering to the Lord, using the same terminology applied to the frankincense on the bread of the Presence.
The priest takes a handful of the grain offering along with all the frankincense and burns it as a memorial (azkara) on the altar, paralleling the function of the bread of the Presence.
The priest burns the memorial portion (azkara) on the altar, following the same ritual practice as with the frankincense on the bread of the Presence.
The bread of the Presence was to remain on the table before the Lord at all times, and this verse explains the associated offering of frankincense.
Solomon made the gold table where the bread of the Presence was to be placed, along with the frankincense, according to Leviticus 24:7.
The Levites were responsible for arranging the bread of the Presence every Sabbath, in accordance with the regulations concerning the offering of frankincense.
The table for the bread of the Presence is listed among the temple furnishings, where the frankincense was to be placed as a memorial offering.
